frase_gancho.texto: A building that was once a military school, an observatory and a residence now tells the story of Mexico as the National Museum of History.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Before it was a museum, this part of the building was a school. After the construction work begun in eighteen forty-one, the castle was adapted as the Military College. It was the setting for the defense of September thirteenth, eighteen forty-seven, which left serious damage to the building. The college did not stay there forever. According to the historian Michael Drewes, in eighteen fifty-eight General Miramón moved the students out. The school returned around eighteen eighty-two. The National Museum of History adds one detail. In eighteen eighty-three the observatory moved to Tacubaya so that the castle could once again be the Military College. The museum era arrived with President Lázaro Cárdenas, who moved his official residence to Los Pinos. On February third, nineteen thirty-nine, it was declared the National Museum of History. It was inaugurated on September twenty-seventh, nineteen forty-four.
